significance.basis: Bridges structural complexity theory with machine-checked verification, providing robust finite guarantees while explicitly identifying the open problem of asymptotic uniform Turing machine mechanization.

strengths: Flawless zero-dependency Lean 4 formalization with 0 sorry, 0 warnings, and 11 zero-axiom theorems.
Comprehensive empirical verification via OUH-CERT-1.0 covering 16 canonical certificates across 4 modes.
Rigorous red-team adversarial test suite achieving 60/60 rejections of invalid forgeries.
Clear, transparent exposition of explicit scope and limitations.
strong_novelty_candidates: Machine-checked exact combinatorial certificates for Krentel lex-max transcripts and dot-operator collapses in input-oblivious unambiguous hierarchies.
summary: This manuscript presents a rigorous, machine-checked formalization in Lean 4.35.0 (18 constructive theorems, 11 zero-axiom, 0 sorry, 0 warnings) of the finite combinatorial core of Edward A. Hirsch's paper on input-oblivious unambiguous hierarchies, accompanied by the pure-stdlib verifier OUH-CERT-1.0 which validates 16 canonical certificates and successfully repels 60/60 red-team adversarial forgeries.
weaknesses: Formalization is restricted to the finite combinatorial and oracle-consistency core; mechanizing asymptotic polynomial-time oracle Turing machines remains open.
